✅ **F-2742-1 — OWNER'S DESK (2026-09-28, from s2742): origin rejects the inheritance history's 108.21 MiB trace.** A normal `git push origin main` returned rc 1 / GH001: historical blob `6e329b47a526bb6ad14ee86877f98b2669ca7606` is 113,467,543 B, above GitHub's 100 MiB limit. Evidence commit `3614d705a` introduced it; `f1a4fb214` removed the file from the tree, but merge `a950f588d` still carries that ancestry. Live origin remains `0979de763`; deployed inheritance `c4953ac7` and subsequent local bookkeeping are not backed up there. The traces remain in git and the existing private local evidence directory. Recommendation: an attended archive-first clean re-land from the last accepted origin tip, preserving the rejected lineage before changing any main pointer, then ordinary push; no force-push and no deletion. GATE: owner authorizes that history repair, rejected lineage preservation is verified, the replacement passes its required gates and origin accepts it. Fires do not repeat unchanged rejected pushes or rewrite this history. Current tdi1 main verification and audio custody remain attended-owned. Decision and options: `docs/OWNER-DESK-2026-09-19.md` §8; evidence `artifacts/s2742/origin-push-failure.txt`, `artifacts/s2742/origin-large-blobs.json`. **Attended 2026-09-28T15:57Z: the clean re-land is BUILT and BACKED UP. In a scratch clone, `git filter-repo --invert-paths` dropped only the five oversized trace-results directories from the 53 unpublished commits since `0979de763`; the new tip's tree is byte-identical to main's, no blob over 100 MB remains, 53 commits preserved, and the lineage is pushed to origin as `candidate/main-repair-2026-09-28b` (tip `23f27b940`), so today's landings are on GitHub now. The rejected lineage is kept locally as `archive/main-rejected-2026-09-28`. The old→new commit map is at `~/.goldrush/repair/commit-map-2026-09-28b.txt`; the re-point pass over every cited id (the A3 precedent) is scripted and dry-run. What waits on your word: moving local `main` onto the candidate (an ordinary fast-forward push, no force-push), the re-point commit, and rebasing lane-b's three unlanded commits. Fires are held during the move.** **s2748 verification (2026-09-28):** live origin confirms candidate `23f27b940`, but its commit-map source is `280956864`, the early s2747 checkpoint. Both trees are `3df9cafafb5dd15b3ad2f7412e062f1d8de6cc35`; this is a backup through that checkpoint, not current main. The later accepted audio test drain `8d08a8c5f` (implementation `6c6c9c268`), its review/evidence and subsequent bookkeeping are absent from the candidate. Lane-b now has zero commits ahead of main; the earlier rebase/landing to-do is superseded. Attended repair must refresh against current main and preserve this accepted drain before any pointer move. Origin main remains `0979de763`; owner gate unchanged. Evidence: `artifacts/s2748/repair-boundary.json`, `artifacts/s2748/candidate-delta.txt`. **Attended refresh (2026-09-29T02:06Z):** candidate REFRESHED against current main as `candidate/main-repair-2026-09-29` (`d7f18e6c6`, 228 commits, tip tree identical to `c5709dcd5`, which carries the s2747 audio drain s2748 named; no blob over 40 MB; map `~/.goldrush/repair/commit-map-2026-09-29.txt`, 229 lines). Main moved again within the minute (s2789's two commits, then the trace-guard master), so the repair no longer consumes a pre-cut candidate: on the owner's **go** the script RE-CUTS from the current main under the fire hold, from a data-derived list (every `-results/` path under the incident dir that is absent from the tip: 25 today), verifies identical tree, same commit count and no blob over 40 MB, backs the cut up as `candidate/main-repair-go-<stamp>`, and only then moves `main` (ordinary push, no force). The cause is being cured at the source by `lane-evidence-trace-guard-1` (lane-d). Owner gate unchanged: go / wait. ✅ DISCHARGED 2026-09-29T06:49Z on the owner's word ("yes, go, move it please", 2026-09-29): `scripts/attended/repair-main.sh` held the fires 04:53Z to 05:59Z, re-cut the clean lineage from the then-current main (`65f128c8a`: identical tip tree, same commit count, no blob over 40 MB, backed up as `candidate/main-repair-go-20260929-0453`), moved `main` by `update-ref` with the old value as guard, re-pointed every cited commit id (commit `4cd9cfc61`: 332 files, 1,149 insertions / 1,022 deletions, same-length ids; 0 residual old prefixes on the ledger surfaces; all 1,127 `mergeHash` values in `tasks/goals.json` resolve in the new history), reset lane-a and lane-b onto the new main (they held only old-lineage commits; lane-c/d were already ancestors), and pushed with an ORDINARY push: `0979de763..4cd9cfc61 main -> main`; origin/main = main, 0 unpushed. The rejected lineage stays under `archive/main-rejected-2026-09-28`. Method note: the regex re-point crawled 1.46 GB of evidence text at ~13 files an hour; a `grep -lF` pre-filter of the 250 changed 7-char prefixes found the 15 unreached files in 33 minutes and `repoint-ids.py --files` finished them in seconds (the option is now in the script); the crawl had rewritten 319. The cause is cured at the source by `lane-evidence-trace-guard-1` (landed `d690cae28`, runner restarted).

🔺 **F-2299-1 — OWNER'S DESK (2026-09-24, from the rotation check after the owner's "Ok, I updaed all the keys"): the rotation's last mile: two new values into `.env.local`, and the Claude Code token still the exposed one.** VERIFIED 2026-09-24 read-only, no value printed or copied: the edge API token in `.env.local` is DEAD at its provider (the token-verify endpoint answers `1000 Invalid API Token`) and the voice key is DEAD (`HTTP 401` on the user endpoint), so both rotations happened at the providers; but `.env.local` was last written 2026-09-20, so the file `scripts/deploy.sh` sources still holds the dead values and **every deploy aborts at the wrangler auth until the owner pastes the new `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=` and `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=` lines** (a failed deploy in a fire log until then is THIS, not a regression; do not file it). The fires' own credential, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (the "coding-agent subscription token" of ruling 1), still authenticates through the fires' exact path (`claude auth status` under `~/.claude-fires` reads loggedIn; a one-word `-p` probe answered), so the value exposed on 2026-08-25 is STILL LIVE: the owner mints a new one (`claude setup-token`), pastes it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=`, and revokes the old one in his account; the attended session re-probes and closes. The droplet holds no stray copy (`find / -name .env.local` empty, `/opt/goldrush/.env.local` absent, read-only over the deploy's own ssh path). The Codex login was refreshed today (`~/.codex/auth.json`, "Logged in using ChatGPT"). Retires when: both new values answer live to the same read-only calls, the Claude probe passes on a NEW value (`.env.local` rewritten) and the owner says the old one is revoked. The original finding is the F-2299-1 row of s2299 below. ➡️ **UPDATE 2026-09-24 18:15 local (owner: "I rotated all tokens in the .env.local file", "I rolled it again"):** the owner rotated all three at the providers and minted a new Claude Code token, but pasted twice into the sibling folder's copy (`Gold Rush-history-local/.env.local`, the pre-rewrite local history), which nothing reads; the attended session found it by mtime, verified its values read-only (Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, the new Claude token answers through the fires' path, per-line hashes: the three rotated lines DIFFERENT, the account id, the router key and the droplet host identical), backed the old root file up outside every git tree (`~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24`, mode 600; a `.bak` beside `.env.local` would NOT be gitignored) and copied the edited file into the repo root; re-verified from the root: Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, Claude `ok`, `wrangler whoami` logged in. DEPLOYS UNBLOCKED. STILL OPEN: the Claude Code token exposed on 2026-08-25 still authenticated at 18:14 when probed from the old file, so it is not revoked; the desk item narrows to that one revocation (the owner's account settings), verified afterwards by the same probe against the backup. ➡️ **UPDATE 2026-09-24 23:2x local (owner, verbatim: "I used the log out of all devices button in the web ui. Then I logged in again, logged in here, then did claude setup-token, copied it in .env.local and then told you done."):** MEASURED, not inferred: after that button, the August token (from the backup) and the 18:13 token (minted before the button) BOTH still answer through the fires' auth path; the button ends browser and CLI sessions (this CLI needed `/login`) but does not revoke long-lived `claude setup-token` tokens. The CLI cannot revoke either (`claude auth logout` clears local credentials only; the only revoke code in the binary is a bundled Google OAuth library; the account endpoints refuse the token with `permission_error`, so its e-mail cannot be read from the token; every login recorded on this Mac is `robin@brainstem.health`, and the fires' config dir dates from 2026-07-08, so the token was minted on or before that day). The newest token (23:16) had again gone to the sibling folder's file; copied into the repo root with the 18:15 root kept at `~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24-1815` (mode 600); root re-verified: Claude ok, Cloudflare active, ElevenLabs 200. REMAINING, owner-side: an Anthropic support request to revoke the Claude Code token minted on or before 2026-07-08 for `robin@brainstem.health` (the exposed one; the 2026-09-24 tokens stay), or its natural expiry; the attended session re-probes from the backup and closes the row when it fails. Exposure bound meanwhile: inference on the owner's subscription only (the account endpoints refuse it). ➡️ **SUPPORT REQUEST ISSUED (owner 2026-09-25, verbatim: "support request is issued"):** the revocation of the August Claude Code token is with Anthropic support; the attended session re-probes the backup token each session (`claude -p ok` under the fires' config from `~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24`) and closes this row, retires the desk item and removes both backup files (owner's word; `rm` prompts) on the first refusal. Until then: live, inference scope only. RULED 2026-09-26 (verbatim "D - as you recommend it"): the attended session keeps re-probing the backup token and retires this row, removing both backup files, on the first refusal.

🔺 **F-2642-3 — OWNER: the registry deploy day is now ACTIONABLE, and the desk entry's own trigger condition has been met.** `docs/OWNER-DESK-2026-09-19.md:100–101` reads *"Astra is landing the registry code behind a closed gate now (lane-b) … I bring you the checklist when the code lands."* **The code has landed (`fdfcab4d0`) and the checklist is `docs/ops/account-registry.md`** — five steps, each with its verification and its rollback sentence. ⚖️ **NOTHING DEPLOYED AND NOTHING MIGRATED, by construction and not by promise: the Pages binding ships as a COMMENTED block in `wrangler.toml` with `ACCOUNT_REGISTRY_SCOPE` deliberately unset, so both are absent and the door behaves byte-identically to main — which `closed-gate.test.mjs` asserts directly rather than by inspection.** Routine Pages deploys are unaffected. ⛔ **NO FIRE MAY ENABLE THIS**: the five steps need the owner's own deployment inventory, a quiesce of every identity writer including previews, an independently verified private export, a migration secret and a post-bootstrap smoke test of legacy saves — none of which the repo can know or automate. It is on the desk, not on the board.

🔺 **F-2299-1 OPEN, NARROWED 2026-09-24 to the Claude Code token and two local pastes (the desk row at the top) — OWNER (s2299 2026-08-25): THE DROPLET SYNC SHIPPED FIVE LIVE CREDENTIALS, AND THE LEAK WAS IN THE RUNBOOK'S OWN RECIPE, NOT THE NEW LEG — CURED ONE LINE, BUT A COPY MAY ALREADY BE ON THE BOX.** Executing F-2298-1's recommendation (a) on a dry board. **Measured LOCAL and READ-ONLY: no ssh to production, nothing deployed, no credential VALUE read, printed or committed.** 🔑 **CORRECTION 1 — THE PAYLOAD IS FIVE CREDENTIALS, NOT ONE.** `.env.local` (428 B, mode 600, untracked, `.gitignore:3`) carries `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — the factory's own Claude subscription credential, i.e. the thing that pays for every fire and every lane runner.** F-2298-1 priced this as "a live Cloudflare token"; the desk was under-informed by four keys. 🔑 **CORRECTION 2, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MOVES THE DECISION — THE LEG IS NOT A DIVERGENCE FROM THE RUNBOOK.** F-2298-1 read `docs/ops/agenttown-server.md:40`'s allowlist and called the denylist a divergence. **The runbook contains BOTH recipes: an allowlist at `:40` and, at `:57`, a denylist that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `deploy.sh:170` after normalising whitespace and `--timeout=60`** (verified by extracting both strings from their files and comparing, not by eye). ➡️ **So the exposure is NOT a defect the new leg introduced — it is a defect in the DOCUMENTED HAND RECIPE, which predates the leg and which the owner may have run at any time since the box was set up. The exposure window is therefore not "since 12:21 today"; it is UNKNOWN.** That is why the cure had to land in BOTH files (fix the CLASS, not the instance). ✅ **PROVEN SENT, THEN PROVEN FIXED, BY MEASUREMENT AND NOT BY READING THE EXCLUDE LIST:** a local `rsync --dry-run` reproducing the leg's exact exclude set — **read out of `deploy.sh` at run time rather than retyped, so the probe cannot drift from its subject** — lists `.env.local` in the transfer set pre-cure and not post-cure; **55,661 → 55,660 files, EXACTLY ONE REMOVED**, which is the whole evidence for "strictly subtractive". ⓘ **The probe asserted its own validity first (F-2215-1) and this was not decorative: its first run returned `0 lines` and REFUSED rather than reporting a clean result, because `rsync -n` prints nothing without an itemiser. A probe whose failure mode is an empty list is indistinguishable from good news.** 🛠️ **CURE: `--exclude .env.local` in `scripts/deploy.sh:170` AND in the runbook's `:57` recipe (`909d8c4ae`). Provably safe: nothing box-side reads that file — `goldrush-assay.service` takes `/etc/goldrush-assay.env` (runbook `:32`), `goldrush-ledger.service` uses `EnvironmentFile=/etc/goldrush-ledger.env` (`:60`), both OUTSIDE the synced tree, which is exactly where the leg's own `sed -i` writes; and `grep -rn "env.local" server/ scripts/assay-worker* scripts/ledger*` returns ZERO hits.** `bash -n scripts/deploy.sh` parses clean. ⚖️ **WHY A FIRE ACTED WHERE s2298 CORRECTLY DID NOT, STATED PLAINLY SO THE OWNER CAN VETO IT: s2298's three reasons were re-measured rather than inherited, and two no longer hold.** Its reason (3) — *"the obvious cure is subtly wrong"* — is about the ALLOWLIST rewrite and **explicitly does not apply to (a)**; its reason (2), *"attended may still be iterating"*, is refuted by measurement (`deploy.sh` unchanged since `3ff1eb606`, clean vs HEAD, 30 min quiet). Only §7.3 remained, and **this is not a deployment act** — it is a one-line subtractive edit to a pipeline script, reversible, inside CLAUDE.md §2's directly-implementable set, taken under §7.4 (owner absent + reversible) with this veto line. **It forecloses nothing: (b) and (c) stay fully open.** 🚨 **WHAT THE CURE DOES NOT DO, AND IT BOUNDS THE OWNER'S REMAINING WORK: rsync PROTECTS excluded names from `--delete` — the same property s2298 used to refute the `node_modules` scare — so if any earlier run of the runbook's `:57` recipe already placed `.env.local` on the box, THIS FIX WILL NOT REMOVE IT.** ❓ **UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: whether a copy is already there needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for.** **One word, and the first half is a two-minute check: (a) `ssh root@<droplet> 'ls -la /opt/goldrush/.env.local'` — if it exists, `rm` it AND ROTATE ALL FIVE CREDENTIALS, because a token that has sat on a public-IP box is disclosed whether or not anyone read it · (b) treat the box as clean on the grounds that the leg never ran and the hand recipe was never used · (c) rotate regardless, as cheap insurance. Recommendation (a) — it is one command and it converts an UNKNOWN into a fact.** ⓘ **Do NOT read this row as closing F-2298-1: the 7.73 GB payload, the allowlist fork, and the missing `ConnectTimeout` on the second `ssh` are all still open there.** Evidence: `artifacts/f2299-1-env-local-exposure/note.md` (reproduce recipe §5, ~10 s, local, no network).
